_comment: The D-14 boundary between tools/convener_ops/registration.py (Python) and app/src/content/render.ts (TypeScript, the toolkit-template renderer a volunteer's browser runs). Both sides compute the same public signup address from a Speaker record's own edition_code, using platform.py's R-5 rule -- 'event_id is edition_code, lower-cased' (tools/convener_ops/platform.py::find_speaker) -- rather than asking a volunteer to type the event id into a public announcement by hand. Wave 1 of this fix round published SIGNUP_BASE with a hand-filled '<event id>' placeholder on the reasoning that no Speaker-to-event-id mapping existed; that reasoning was wrong -- R-5 is that mapping, and eventkeys.py's 'no Identifier type exists yet' remark is a claim about a missing TYPE, not about the mapping itself. 'edition_code' is deliberately mixed-case and zero-padded across these cases, since lower-casing IS the rule under test: a case that only ever sees already-lower-case input would not catch a renderer that forgot to lower-case. Task 6: registration left the operators' application's own /signup/:eventId route for an island mounted on the public event page, so the address below now targets that page (site/src/event.njk's permalink, /events/<id>/, D-19) instead of the retired app route.
